paper_title: Stochastic fluctuations of bosonic dark matter
suggested_experiment_name: Stochastic reanalysis of axion-nucleon DM constraints (CASPEr-ZULF / nEDM et al.)
notes: This is a theoretical/methodological paper, not a new experimental search. It shows that previous bosonic DM constraints (nEDM, CASPEr-ZULF-Comagnetometer, CASPEr-ZULF-Sidebands for axion-nucleon coupling gaNN; clock/spectroscopy experiments for dilaton d_e) were overestimated by factors of ~3-10 (specifically ~8.4 for pseudoscalar wind searches, ~2.7-3.0 for scalar couplings) because they ignored stochastic amplitude fluctuations of the virialized ultralight field in the T << tau_c regime. The modified exclusion plots (Fig. 3 for gaNN in GeV^-1, Fig. 4 for dilaton couplings) are rescalings of previously published limits, not new measurements, and no numerical limit tables are provided. The pre-analysis hint of AxionEDM appears incorrect: the main exclusion plot is for the axion-nucleon gradient coupling gaNN (nEDM is one of the corrected experiments, but the plotted quantity is gaNN). Assumed local DM density in the underlying analyses is 0.4 GeV/cm^3, but no data points are extracted here.
